1.

A childlike spirit of obedience Is not found in everyone Of those who here confess Themselves to believe in the Saviour; For the sweet yoke of Jesus One must take upon oneself, Subdue the self-will And find rest for the heart.

2.

If suffering and reproach On the way meet us here, Ah, remember it is God’s love That thus teaches us obedience, And deeper becomes the joy To obey the Lord’s commandments, If we on the altar-height Have received testimony from God.

3.

Surely Jeremiah laments That he is shut in And in the days of sorrow Pressed on every side; But every trial becomes A high Jacob’s ladder, On which the soul ascends To God with all its need.

4.

Have comfort then, pilgrim band, For we are reminded indeed That the water in Marah Was bitter before as now; But see, who is that tree Which was cast into its stream? Yes, it is Jesus Christ, Who for us suffered and died.

5.

And mark, His obedience He learned Through what He suffered; God set value thereon, He became the “Captain of salvation.” At the thought of His love, Which has suffered and died, Affliction, sorrow, and reproach, Our Marah-water, becomes sweet.
